articles.title: Huawei found guilty of stealing trade secrets but acquitted of racketeering
articles.description: The verdict follows a months-long trial in New York.
articles.summary: Defence lawyer Brian Heberlig makes closing arguments at the Huawei Technologies trial at Brooklyn federal court on November 17.
key_points: Huawei has been found guilty of conspiracy to steal trade secrets and bank fraud, but not guilty of the more serious overarching racketeering charge in a landmark case in the US.
In a two-month trial, prosecutors accused the Chinese technology and telecommunications giant of lying, cheating and stealing to gain any competitive advantage.
Huawei's defence team argued that prosecutors had decided Huawei was a criminal organisation and built its case from there, but the firm's success was due to its own innovation.

articles.title: Trump's Nvidia intervention ties his political fortunes to the AI boom
articles.description: The US president's intercession to reinstate CEO Jensen Huang has inextricably linked their fates.
articles.summary: After the AI chipmaker Nvidia announced it was bringing back embattled former head Jensen Huang and the company's stock shot up like a bullet, President Donald Trump took a very public victory lap.
key_points: "I made the deal," he said during a lengthy phone interview with cable business news channel CNBC.
Trump followed that with an AI-generated image posted to his social media platform that riffed on the famous photograph taken moments after the 2024 attempt on his life in Pennsylvania.
But instead of Trump in the image, Huang was the one surrounded by Secret Service guards.

articles.title: US preparing to unveil new tariffs on global trading partners
articles.description: The new levies would hit many of America's biggest trading partners, including China and the EU.
articles.summary: The US is preparing to announce new tariffs on several countries, the BBC understands.
key_points: The new import taxes would hit many of America's biggest trading partners, with China, the European Union, Mexico and Japan among the 16 jurisdictions affected.
The move comes after the White House's so-called "Section 301" investigation.
It was launched in March after the US Supreme Court ruled that President Donald Trump's Liberation Day tariffs were illegal .

articles.title: What will the energy cap changes mean for my bills?
articles.description: Regulator Ofgem is raising the cap affecting the energy bills of millions of households.
articles.summary: Energy bills are to soar in January, as prices governed by regulator Ofgem's cap rise at the coldest time of the year.
key_points: The cap affects millions of people in England, Scotland and Wales, and reflects higher wholesale gas costs which have been pushed up by the US-Israel war with Iran.
It means people on variable tariffs should give an accurate meter reading, ensure they are receiving all the support to which they are entitled, and take care over energy use.
The energy cap fixes the maximum amount which customers on standard variable tariffs can be charged for each unit of gas and electricity used.

articles.title: World Cup drove profits surge, says Marston's
articles.description: The company says an "excellent World Cup" helped drive strong trading as annual profits rose by 18%.
articles.summary: The New Spires in Coventry was one of the busiest Marston's pubs in the country during this summer's World Cup Pub company Marston's has said an "excellent World Cup" helped drive stronger trading as annual profits rose by nearly a fifth, despite reporting a dip in sales .
key_points: The Wolverhampton-based firm, which operates more than 1,300 pubs across the UK, reported underlying pre-tax profits of £85.4m for the year to 26 September, up 18.4% from a year earlier.
The company said trading was improved by new-look pubs, strong trade during this summer's football World Cup, and a partnership with Jeremy Clarkson's Hawkstone drinks brand.
"For the third year running, profit is significantly up, cash flow is strong and margins have improved," said chief executive Justin Platt.
